 YUSUF SADIK MOHAMMAD TARAJIYA  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
MR ZUBIN F BHARDA(159) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 DS AFF.NOT FILED (N) for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR DHAWAN JAYSWAL, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT  Date : 21/07/2023  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By way of present application, under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant seeks quashment of the impugned FIR being CR-I No.7 of 2019 registered with the Maroli Police Station, District : Navsari for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The brief facts of the prosecution case are that the applicant has made forged documents i.e. false death certificate, concocted power of attorney and fabricated pedigree of the persons who are residing in South Africa since long and treated to be true documents, used in mutating the revenue entries and thereby tried to snatch away the lands NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/625/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/07/2023 undefined in question and thereby committed an offence as alleged in the complaint.
Hence, this complaint against the applicant and others.
3. Heard learned advocates.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the applicants has submitted that no prima facie case is made out against the applicant.
He has submitted that this is purely a civil dispute and the complainant has given criminal colour.
He has submitted that this is nothing but abuse of process of law.
He has submitted that the applicant and the complainant are the near relatives.
He has submitted that it is a family dispute in fact.
He has also submitted that the complainant has wrongly roped the applicant in the alleged offence.
He has submitted that the applicant has not made any false or fabricated documents or signatures as alleged in the complaint.
He has submitted that neither the ingredients of cheating nor criminal breach of trust are disclosed from the bare reading of the FIR.

He has submitted that the complainant clearly discloses that the applicant is a victim of the calculated fraud practiced by the complainant who has prepared false pedigree and false death certificates and declared all the legal heirs of the original owner Ibrahim Ahemad Motara as dead even though two of the five legal NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/625/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/07/2023 undefined heirs are very much alive and are residing in South Africa.

4.2 He has submitted that the complainant has made many civil as well as revenue litigation against the applicant and others and since he failed in those litigation, he took aid of the criminal litigation and applied pressurised tactics.
He has submitted that the complainant has challenged the same to get the handsome amount from the applicant since the prices of the lands are sky-rocketed.
He has submitted that this Court may exercise the powers in favour of the applicant under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
He has submitted that this application may be allowed.
5. Per contra, learned APP for the State has submitted that there is a prima facie case against the applicant.
He has submitted that the applicant has created forged documents and thereby tried to snatch away the precious lands of the complainant and committed an offence.
He has submitted that this is not a fit case where this Court should exercise the powers under Section 482 of the Code in favour of the applicant.

He has submitted that looking to the entire complaint as well as entire investigation prima facie, it appears that the applicant has committed an offence and therefore, at this stage, this application may not be entertained.
He has submitted that this Court should NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/625/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/07/2023 undefined exercise the powers very sparingly in favour of the applicant at this stage.
He has submitted that this application may be rejected.
6. I have heard rival contentions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties.
I have also perused the documents available on record.

Considering the submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties and also considering the documents available on record, the following factors are weighed with this Court for consideration of this application.
Investigation is over qua the applicant and charge-sheet has already been filed qua the applicant and the Criminal Case is going on before the learned trial Court and is at the stage of evidence.
The original land owners are residing in South Africa and they are origin of this country.
By passage of time, the prices of the lands in question are sky-rocketed.

sentences.text: 2  The applicant as well as other persons are very well aware about the fact that the original land owners are not residing in India since long.
There are civil as well as revenue litigation between the parties.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/625/2020 ORDER DATED: 21/07/2023 undefined
The documents in questions have been sent to the FSL, Gandhinagar by the Investigating Officer and report is awaited.
It is not that the complainant has not taken any action about the alleged forged.
He has immediately taken the aid of the law.
Some accused are arrested and enlarged on bail and some are still wanted.
The complainant has run from pillar to post.
Let the trial be proceeded against the applicant.

8. In view of the settled position of law and after considering the facts stated in the FIR and circumstances of the present case, it transpires that the fruitful purpose would be served if such further proceedings are allowed to be continued.
Let the applicants be faced the trial.
When prima facie ingredients of offence is made out in the complaint, the complaint cannot be quashed, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court time and again.
Even otherwise, this Court has very limited powers under Section 482 of the Code to quash the complaint.
This application, therefore, needs to be dismissed and is dismissed.
Notice is discharged.
Interim relief stands vacated.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) M.H. DAVE Yusuf Sadik Mohammad Tarajiya vs State Of Gujarat on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44083673/
